events.title: The death of Pope John Paul I
events.shortBlurb: Albino Luciani, the smiling pope of thirty-three days, died in the night in the Apostolic Palace, and 1978 became the year of three popes…
body: Albino Luciani, born in 1912 at Forno di Canale in the Veneto, had been bishop of Vittorio Veneto and then patriarch of Venice before the conclave of 26 August 1978 elected him pope. He was the first to join two names — John Paul, for the two popes he honored — and the first to refuse the tiara, taking a simple inauguration on 3 September.

In the night of 28 September, thirty-three days after his election, he died suddenly in his apartment in the Apostolic Palace; he was found lifeless in his bed at first light of the 29th, and the Holy See reckons his death to the 28th. The medical reconstruction concludes an acute myocardial infarction, and the conspiracy theories that flourished in the absence of an autopsy have collapsed under the evidence since published.

The world mourned 'the smiling pope' and laid him in the Vatican grottoes; in October the cardinals gave the Church John Paul II. His cause advanced quietly, and on 4 September 2022 Pope Francis beatified him in St. Peter's Square.

sources.text: Vatican biography of Pope John Paul I (vatican.va)
